purpose: Current-paper analysis specifications consolidated from versioned contract/repair/scope records. Historical standalone files remain in Git history and release/history branches.

north_america.sampling_unit: standardized route stop conditional on at least one calling species
north_america.response: mean species richness per active stop; excess richness equals alpha_active - 1

existing_authorized_result.direction: wetter member has greater active-unit taxonomic depth

rainfall_exposure.definition: zscore(log1p(number of complete coordinate-local calendar days immediately preceding the repaired event date until the first day with >=1 mm precipitation, capped at 30 days))

australia.primary_response: excess_richness = species_richness - 1; all retained FrogID recordings already have richness >= 1

primary_model.formula: excess_richness ~ dry_z + C(state) * C(month) + year_z + sin_hour + cos_hour

sensitivities.recorder_cluster: same primary OLS formula clustered by recorder
sensitivities.within_cell: demeaned within-ERA5-cell OLS using dry_z, year_z, month indicators, sin_hour and cos_hour; support if beta_dry_z < 0 and complete 95% CI < 0

secondary_endpoints_no_gate: threeplus = I(species_richness >= 3), logistic model with the same covariates and ERA5-cell clustering
excess_beyond_two = max(species_richness - 2, 0), OLS with the same covariates and ERA5-cell clustering

cross_system_decision.pass: Australian primary continuous-depth support AND frozen NAAMP active-alpha 95% CI > 0.
cross_system_decision.strong_pass: PASS plus both Australian continuous-depth sensitivities have 95% CIs below zero.
cross_system_decision.reason: The systems use different rainfall-exposure scales and observation designs; comparison is directional on a shared active-unit taxonomic-depth estimand.

interpretation_boundaries: Cross-continental consistency is not worldwide universality.
FrogID recordings and NAAMP stops are different observation systems.
The result concerns behaviourally realized acoustic richness conditional on acoustic activity, not occupancy or abundance.
The North American four-component species x stop matrix geometry cannot be replicated in FrogID because FrogID lacks fixed ten-stop route matrices.
The historical >=2-species conditional discrepancy remains part of the record and is not overwritten.

triggers.eventtime_semantics_audit: all 655,502 events carry explicit UTC offsets

unchanged.era5_source: Earthmover public Icechunk ERA5 single/temporal tp
unchanged.primary_formula: multi ~ dry_z + C(state) * C(month) + year_z + sin_hour + cos_hour

timing_repair.timestamp: combine eventDate with offset-bearing eventTime and parse as an aware ISO-8601 instant
timing_repair.repaired_event_date: calendar date after converting the aware event instant to the coordinate timezone
timing_repair.repaired_event_hour: fractional clock hour after the same conversion
timing_repair.rainfall_exposure: count complete coordinate-local calendar days immediately before repaired_event_date; event day remains excluded
timing_repair.no_offset_inference: do not infer or overwrite the supplied offset before conversion

transport_rule.rationale: a few local-date corrections may move boundary hours by one day; this is transport-only and may not be tuned to the effect

payload.interpretation_rule: Report repaired result regardless of direction or significance. Original result remains historical; repaired result becomes the submission value if the implementation passes frozen structural checks.
prohibited: no subset selection by repaired effect

payload.question: Can recorded hearing impairment, major-noise interruptions, or wind differences explain the rainfall-associated expansion of the active frog community?
payload.sample: same complete 10-stop matched wetter-drier route x RunNumber pairs as the metacommunity synthesis, restricted only by prespecified detection-covariate availability

stop_hearing_impairment.definition: If Massachusetts MassNoiseIndex is present, impaired=1 for index >=2 and 0 for index 0-1; otherwise use the regional Noise yes/no field when valid (1=yes, 0=no).
stop_hearing_impairment.protocol_basis: NAAMP regional programs could record ambient noise as yes/no or with the Massachusetts noise index; index >=2 corresponds to moderately or more strongly affecting sampling.

stop_timeout.definition: TimeOut==1 if a major noise disturbance caused the observer to break the 5-minute listening period; otherwise 0.

run_wind.definition: mean of numeric StartWind and EndWind Beaufort codes when both are available and within 0-5

run_level_derivation.hearing_impairment_fraction: mean standardized impairment indicator across the 10 sampled stops; require >=8 valid stops
run_level_derivation.timeout_fraction: mean TimeOut across 10 sampled stops; require >=8 valid stops
run_level_derivation.pair_covariates: wet minus dry for each run-level quantity

primary_models.formula: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + hearing_impairment_difference + timeout_difference + wind_difference + C(State) + C(RunNumber)

car_count_2006plus.run_metric: mean numeric CarCount across sampled stops; require >=8 valid stops
car_count_2006plus.model: add wet-minus-dry mean car count to all three primary formulas

mass_noise_index.run_metric: mean MassNoiseIndex among valid 0-4 values; require >=8 valid stops
mass_noise_index.model: replace standardized hearing-impairment fraction with wet-minus-dry mean MassNoiseIndex while retaining timeout and wind

interpretation.if_supported: The rainfall-associated spatial, local-alpha and route-gamma signals are not explained by recorded survey hearing impairment, noise interruptions or wind differences.
interpretation.boundary: This is a measured-detection-condition robustness test, not proof that all acoustic detectability differences are absent.

prohibited: no outcome-dependent choice among noise encodings
no changing MassNoiseIndex threshold after readback
no excluding noisy surveys based on observed effect direction

payload.ecological_question: Does recent rainfall expand the acoustically active frog community by recruiting additional species around a persistent route-level core, or by replacing species through turnover?
payload.biological_hypothesis: Rainfall acts as a short environmental pulse that relaxes constraints on reproductive acoustic activity, producing nested expansion of the active community rather than wholesale compositional turnover.

eligibility.temperature: >=8 valid stop temperatures and run mean in [-10,45] C

pairing.rule: Within each stratum, sort eligible runs by SurveyYear and pair adjacent observed years. A run may contribute to at most two adjacent pairs.
pairing.orientation: For pairs with unequal DaysSinceRain, define the run with lower DaysSinceRain as the wetter run and the other as the drier run. Equal-rain pairs are excluded.

community_metrics.shared: number of species active in both runs
community_metrics.wet_only: number active only in wetter run
community_metrics.dry_only: number active only in drier run
community_metrics.gain_share: wet_only/(wet_only + dry_only), defined when discordant species >0
community_metrics.dry_core_retention: shared/(shared + dry_only), defined when drier-run richness >0

primary_models.richness_gain: OLS with cluster-robust SE by State:RouteNumber; richness_gain ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber)
primary_models.nestedness_component: OLS with same predictors and clustering
primary_models.simpson_turnover: OLS with same predictors and clustering

descriptive_support.gain_loss_balance: Report total wet_only and dry_only counts across pairs and mean gain_share. This is descriptive because species discordances are not independent.
descriptive_support.dry_core_retention: Report mean and median retention of drier-run active species in wetter runs.

prediction.P1: Greater rainfall contrast predicts positive richness_gain.
prediction.P2: Greater rainfall contrast predicts increased nestedness_component.
prediction.P3: Greater rainfall contrast does not require increased simpson_turnover; a null or weaker turnover slope together with P1/P2 supports nested expansion.
prediction.P4: Across matched pairs, wetter runs retain a large fraction of the drier-run active species while adding more species than they lose.

interpretation_boundary: This analysis concerns acoustically active community composition, not census abundance or occupancy.
Calling activity is a reproductive-behaviour proxy and does not by itself establish breeding success.
The ecological extension is post-opening relative to the original rain endpoint and is not part of the original confirmatory family.
No causal rainfall claim is authorized.

payload.purpose: Audit geographic transportability of the already-authorized RC6 headline; not a new ecological endpoint or mechanism search.
payload.population: The existing 4,236 matched wetter-drier NAAMP comparisons from 585 routes in 21 states.

state_specific_slopes.model: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(RunNumber)
state_specific_slopes.interpretation: Direction and effect-size distribution; individual-state significance is not a pass criterion.

leave_one_state_out.model: original RC6 model response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber)
leave_one_state_out.pass_rule: For each of the three headline responses, all leave-one-state-out rain_contrast coefficients remain positive.
leave_one_state_out.strong_pass_rule: All leave-one-state-out 95% confidence intervals remain above zero for all three headline responses.

state_random_slope.model_family: linear mixed model with State random intercept and rain_contrast random slope; fixed rain_contrast + temperature difference + day-of-year difference + year gap + RunNumber
state_random_slope.role: Quantify geographic heterogeneity; no requirement that every state-specific slope is positive.

decision_language.pass: The RC6 expansion signal is not driven by any single state and is geographically transportable across the sampled NAAMP region, while allowing state-level effect heterogeneity.
decision_language.fail: The continent-scale association remains supported in the pooled matched analysis, but geographic consistency is limited because at least one state materially controls a headline coefficient.
prohibited: the effect occurs in every state
state-specific P<0.05 as a requirement for generality

secondary: mean pairwise Simpson turnover among active stops
mean pairwise nestedness-resultant dissimilarity among active stops

model.formula: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber)

interpretation_boundary.metacommunity: behaviourally realized acoustic metacommunity, not occupancy metacommunity

payload.sample: the existing 4,236 matched wet-dry route x RunNumber pairs used by the RC9 four-component decomposition
payload.question: Does the observed incidence allocation still depart from uniform activation when the null strongly preserves pair-specific dry species x stop occupancy and removes hierarchical shrinkage toward species means?
payload.candidate_species_pool: For each State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum, use the same full eligible-run union of species as the existing uniform-activation null. This retains nonzero opportunity for combinations seen only outside dry history.

historical_cell_probability.data: unique drier-member runs within the matched dataset, each RunID counted once
historical_cell_probability.rationale: Avoid the reviewer concern that shrinkage toward species means weakens stable species x stop identity.

pair_specific_persistence.formula: p_anchor=(1-a)*p_hist + a*I(cell present in the observed drier member)
pair_specific_persistence.interpretation: At a=0.90, dry-present cells start near one and dry-absent cells near zero before the common shift, providing an intentionally persistence-favouring stress test.

payload.uniform_activation: For each matched pair, apply one common additive log-odds shift delta to all anchored cell probabilities and solve delta so expected wet incidence count equals that pair's observed wet incidence count.

simulation.wet_cells: independent Bernoulli draws from the shifted anchored probabilities
simulation.quadrants: the exact corner-expansion, spatial-spread, taxonomic-deepening and within-core-rearrangement net components against the fixed observed dry matrix

primary_test.statistic: Mahalanobis distance of the observed four-component rainfall-contrast coefficient vector from the simulated-null mean using simulated covariance
primary_test.reject_rule: Monte Carlo p < 0.05 at anchor weight a=0.75

robustness_rule.inconclusive: primary a=0.75 rejects but either a=0.50 or a=0.90 does not

title_support_rule.boundary_biased_title_authorized: strong_rejection AND observed boundary-crossing share exceeds the upper 95% null bound at a=0.75
title_support_rule.candidate_title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities is more boundary-biased than uniform activation predicts

secondary_reports: null mean and 95% interval for each four-component coefficient share
null mean and 95% interval for boundary crossing
comparison of expected within-core share with the existing kappa=2 null

interpretation_boundary.rejection: Evidence that the observed allocation is not captured even by a uniform-activation process that strongly favours persistence of pair-specific dry cells. It does not identify a unique mechanism.
interpretation_boundary.ecological_hypothesis_if_rejected: Low-dry-frequency species x stop combinations may be disproportionately recruited under recent-rain conditions; temporary or intermittently suitable wet sites are one plausible discussion-level explanation, not an identified mechanism.

payload.reason: The NAAMP national protocol states that Gulf Coast and Great Plains routes should have been conducted within three days of rainfall. This sensitivity asks whether the existing RC7 footprint/alpha/gamma associations remain when rainfall contrast extends beyond that protocol-target window.
payload.model: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), route-clustered covariance

primary_crosses_three_day_window.meaning: At least the drier member lies outside the protocol-target 0-3 day post-rain window.
primary_crosses_three_day_window.pass_rule: All three rainfall-contrast coefficients are positive.
primary_crosses_three_day_window.strong_pass_rule: All three 95% confidence intervals are entirely above zero.

secondary_both_outside_three_day_window.meaning: Both members lie outside the protocol-target 0-3 day post-rain window.
secondary_both_outside_three_day_window.decision_role: descriptive diagnostic only; report n, slopes and confidence intervals without a PASS requirement because this subset may remove the biologically strongest immediate-rain contrasts.

authorized_interpretation.primary_pass: The multiscale association is not confined to comparisons entirely within the 0-3 day protocol-target window.
authorized_interpretation.primary_strong_pass: The footprint, alpha and gamma associations remain confidence-interval positive when the drier survey lies outside the 0-3 day protocol-target window.
authorized_interpretation.primary_fail: The pooled RC7 association remains the headline, but evidence outside the protocol-target window is insufficient or directionally inconsistent.

prohibited: the sensitivity identifies which states followed the rainfall-targeting protocol
a failed both-outside diagnostic invalidates the primary matched result

payload.question: Does the RC10 rainfall-associated expansion and boundary-biased incidence allocation persist when wetter-drier comparisons are restricted to the same recorded NAAMP observer?

sample.base: same complete 10-stop matched wetter-drier route x RunNumber pairs as RC10
sample.restriction: ObserverTrackingID must be nonempty and identical for the wetter and drier run

minimum_gate.action_if_failed: report coverage and retain observer turnover as a limitation; do not interpret inferential endpoints

payload.headline_models: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), cluster-robust by State x RouteNumber

primary_uniform_null.magnitude_matching: match each wetter run's observed species x stop incidence count

classification.observer_robust: minimum gate passes; all three headline rain-contrast coefficients are positive with 95% CIs excluding zero; the four-component omnibus rejects at P<0.05 for primary kappa=2 and primary anchor=0.75; and observed boundary crossing lies above the 95% null interval for both primary nulls
classification.directionally_consistent_qualified: minimum gate passes and all three headline coefficients are positive, while observed boundary crossing exceeds both primary null means, but one or more strong-support conditions above fail
classification.mixed: minimum gate passes but headline signs differ or observed boundary crossing does not exceed one or both primary null means

interpretation_boundary.purpose: address observer-turnover detectability as a reviewer robustness concern without changing the frozen RC10 story

payload.context: The conventional Sørensen coefficient and 95% CI were already known in RC7; this is therefore a bounded robustness test, not a preregistered equivalence analysis.
payload.response: wet-minus-dry mean pairwise Sørensen dissimilarity among active stops
payload.model: delta_sorensen ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), cluster-robust by State x RouteNumber
payload.margin_rationale: 2.5 percentage points on the bounded 0-1 Sørensen dissimilarity scale per unit log-rainfall contrast; deliberately tighter than the existing +/-0.05 matrix-fill margin.
payload.decision_rule: practical equivalence if the complete 90% confidence interval for the rainfall-contrast coefficient lies within [-0.025,+0.025]
payload.sensitivity: apply the identical margin and rule to exact consecutive-year pairs
payload.title_support_rule: equivalence wording for Sørensen is authorized only if both the primary and exact-consecutive-year analyses pass

sample.source: same complete 10-stop, temperature-qualified NAAMP runs and adjacent-observed-year route x RunNumber matched pairs as the ecological pulse analysis
sample.pair_orientation: lower DaysSinceRain = wet; higher DaysSinceRain = dry
sample.stop_alignment: same StopNumber within matched route; fail closed unless all 10 stop numbers align

payload.ecological_question: Does rainfall-associated expansion of route-level active species richness arise because the active spatial footprint expands, because species composition changes within already-active stops, or both?

frozen_primary_endpoints.name: delta_active_stops
frozen_primary_endpoints.definition: number of stops with >=1 calling species in wet run minus dry run

frozen_primary_endpoints.name: shared_species_delta_stops_mean
frozen_primary_endpoints.definition: within each pair, mean wet-minus-dry number of occupied stops among species present somewhere in both runs

frozen_primary_endpoints.name: footprint_dependent_net_species
frozen_primary_endpoints.definition: wet-only route species detected exclusively at stops inactive in the dry run, minus dry-only route species detected exclusively at stops inactive in the wet run
frozen_primary_endpoints.meaning: conservative component of route richness change structurally dependent on expansion/contraction of the active-stop footprint

frozen_primary_endpoints.name: within_footprint_net_species
frozen_primary_endpoints.definition: remaining wet-only route species minus remaining dry-only route species after footprint-dependent species are removed
frozen_primary_endpoints.prediction: reported without a directional support gate
frozen_primary_endpoints.meaning: route richness change occurring at least partly within stops already active in the comparison run

payload.exact_identity: richness_gain = footprint_dependent_net_species + within_footprint_net_species for every matched pair
secondary_diagnostics: 2x2 counts of wet incidence gains: route-new versus route-existing species x dry-inactive versus dry-active stop

model.formula: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber)

interpretation_boundary.active: acoustically detected calling activity, not occupancy or abundance
interpretation_boundary.footprint_dependent: structural dependence in the observed stop x species matrix, not causal proof that spatial activation caused species recruitment
interpretation_boundary.rainfall: observational association; no causal rainfall claim
interpretation_boundary.multiplicity: finite decomposition family fixed before endpoint readback; no outcome-dependent retuning

payload.sample: the existing 4,236 matched wet-dry route x RunNumber pairs
payload.question: Are the observed four incidence-component slopes and near-zero Sørensen slope distinguishable from a simple uniform activation process that preserves dry-side species x stop propensities?

null_model.candidate_species_pool: For each State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum, use the union of species detected in any eligible run in that stratum. Using the full long-term stratum pool is conservative because the null is allowed to generate species seen only in wetter surveys.
null_model.dry_history: Use unique drier-member RunIDs from the matched-pair dataset within each stratum. Each unique dry run contributes once.

baseline_probability.hierarchy: For each stratum, estimate a stratum incidence mean, then a species mean, then a species x StopNumber probability from dry-side detections only.
baseline_probability.formula: mu0=(all dry incidences + 0.5)/(n_dry_runs*10*n_species + 1); mu_species=(species dry incidences + kappa*mu0)/(n_dry_runs*10 + kappa); p_cell=(cell dry detections + kappa*mu_species)/(n_dry_runs + kappa)

null_model.uniform_activation: For each matched pair, hold the observed dry matrix fixed. Apply one common additive log-odds shift delta to every candidate species x stop cell. Solve delta so that the expected number of simulated wet incidences equals that pair's observed wet incidence count. This conditions the null on response magnitude in expectation and tests allocation/geometry rather than total activation.

simulation.wet_cells: independent Bernoulli draws from the shifted probabilities
simulation.quadrants: recompute the exact RC7 corner-expansion, spatial-spread, taxonomic-deepening and within-core-rearrangement net components against the fixed observed dry matrix
simulation.beta: recompute mean pairwise Sørensen dissimilarity among active stops and fit the same wet-minus-dry rainfall-contrast slope

primary_test.statistic: Mahalanobis distance of the observed five-element vector from the simulated-null mean using the simulated covariance matrix
primary_test.p_value: Monte Carlo upper-tail fraction of simulated Mahalanobis distances at least as large as the observed distance

robustness_rule.inconclusive: kappa=2 rejects but either kappa=1 or kappa=5 does not

secondary_reports: null mean and 95% interval for each of the four coefficient shares
null mean and 95% interval for the boundary-crossing share = 1 - within-core share
null mean and 95% interval for the Sørensen rain-contrast beta

interpretation_boundary.uniform_activation: a common log-odds activation shift on dry-side acoustic detection propensities; not a demographic model
interpretation_boundary.rejecting_null: evidence that the observed allocation is not captured by this simple uniform-activation model; not proof of a unique biological mechanism
interpretation_boundary.failing_to_reject: the matrix allocation is statistically consistent with simple uniform activation and must not be sold as a distinct structured mechanism

payload.question: When active-stop mean species richness rises with rainfall contrast, is that due to crossing from one to at least two species, or to additional species beyond the second within already multispecies stops?

exact_decomposition.coefficient_identity: OLS rain-contrast beta for delta mean richness must equal the sum of component betas under identical rows/covariates

primary_endpoints.role: local taxonomic deepening holding active-stop membership fixed

secondary_diagnostics: same-stop transition counts among shared-active stops: 1->1, 1->2, 1->3plus, 2plus->1, 2->2, 2->3plus, 3plus->lower, 3plus->same_or_higher
newly-active-stop mean species count in wet run
lost-active-stop mean species count in dry run

models.formula: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber)

interpretation_boundary.active_stop: acoustic detection, not occupancy or abundance
interpretation_boundary.shared_active_stop: same numbered route stop active in both surveys; not repeated-measures proof of local population change

payload.reason: The four incidence components are defined for all 4,236 matched pairs, whereas pairwise Sørensen is conditional on both runs having at least two active stops. A single joint Mahalanobis vector would mix different estimands or require conditioning the incidence null on beta-diversity eligibility.

primary_uniform_activation_test.statistic: Mahalanobis distance from the simulated four-component null
primary_uniform_activation_test.decision_rules: unchanged p<0.05 primary; strong rejection requires p<0.05 for kappa=1,2,5

secondary_sorensen_null.sample: the same fixed pair set on which the observed Sørensen wet-minus-dry response is defined
secondary_sorensen_null.simulation: simulate under the same uniform-activation probabilities; for each eligible pair, resample simulated wet matrices until at least two stops are active so the beta-diversity estimand remains defined
secondary_sorensen_null.report: null mean, 95% interval and observed percentile for the Sørensen rain-contrast beta
secondary_sorensen_null.note: The secondary Sørensen null is simulated only for the primary smoothing specification kappa=2; kappa=1 and 5 are reserved for the four-component geometry sensitivity.

repair.headline_homogenization_decision: Use the separately frozen Sørensen practical-equivalence analysis, not the uniform-null omnibus.

payload.reason: Pre-submission review identified three remaining risks: the title overweights post hoc Sorensen equivalence, FrogID wording can sound like blinded external validation despite earlier positive FrogID multiplicity results, and the uniform-activation null may underrepresent strong species x stop persistence because historical cell probabilities are hierarchically shrunk.
authorized_changes: Add one persistence-preserving uniform-activation sensitivity family, frozen before endpoint readback.
Demote FrogID wording from independent/external validation to cross-dataset directional consistency while retaining the already frozen estimates.
Move practical Sorensen non-homogenization out of the title and make incidence allocation versus uniform activation the title-level result.
Compress robustness-method prose to Supporting Information if needed for JAE word count.
not_authorized: post-readback retuning of the persistence null
payload.scientific_goal: Test whether the observed four-component allocation remains unusual when the null strongly preserves the pair-specific dry species x stop state.

always.frogid_wording: Use cross-dataset consistency / directional agreement across two monitoring datasets. Do not call the continuous-depth analysis an independent test or external validation.
always.sorensen_title: Remove without practical homogenization from the title. Keep post hoc practical-equivalence as a secondary bounded result in Results/Discussion.
always.worldwide_wording: Do not claim worldwide, universal or global generality.

if_strong_rejection_and_boundary_above_p.title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities is more boundary-biased than uniform activation predicts
if_strong_rejection_and_boundary_above_p.main_interpretation: The allocation departure survives a persistence-favouring null, strengthening the claim that uniform amplification does not reproduce where additional participation enters the matrix.
if_strong_rejection_and_boundary_above_p.discussion: May discuss preferential recruitment of combinations rare in dry conditions and temporary/intermittent wet-site activation as plausible hypotheses, explicitly non-causal.

if_primary_rejects_but_not_strong.title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities departs from uniform activation
if_primary_rejects_but_not_strong.main_interpretation: Structured departure is retained but persistence sensitivity is qualified.

if_primary_does_not_reject.title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities across spatial and taxonomic scales
if_primary_does_not_reject.main_interpretation: Do not claim allocation beyond uniform activation as a robust headline; retain original null as model-dependent evidence.

payload.reason: Test whether the most generalizable component of RC8—taxonomic deepening within already-active sampling units—shows the same rainfall-associated direction in independent North American and Australian monitoring systems.
authorized_new_endpoint_family: Australian FrogID continuous taxonomic depth within already-active recordings, using the already frozen FrogID sample and timezone-repaired ERA5 dry-spell exposure.
Cross-system directional comparison against the already authorized NAAMP local-alpha result among active stops.
not_authorized: replacement of the RC8 North American matrix-geometry test

promotion_rule.cross_continental_consistency: Authorized only if the Australian primary continuous-depth coefficient is negative with its complete 95% CI below zero, while the already frozen NAAMP active-alpha coefficient remains positive with its complete 95% CI above zero.
promotion_rule.strong_cross_continental_consistency: Additionally requires the Australian recorder-clustered and within-ERA5-cell continuous-depth sensitivities to have negative coefficients with complete 95% CIs below zero.
promotion_rule.failure: If the Australian primary gate fails, retain FrogID as a historical differently conditioned contrast and do not add cross-continental generality to the RC8 headline.

payload.wording_boundary: Even a strong pass authorizes cross-continental consistency across independent North American and Australian monitoring systems, not a world-wide or universal response.
